items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: I called Kenny Barron and I called Louis Nash... I said, “I’ve got Kenny Barron, Ron Carter and Louis Nash.” She gave me a week.

ctx.x: Have you had potential managers or club owners who would say to you, well if you only did more, you know, organ trio type stuff or if you had a little more, put some reggae into your act, or tried to insert musical decisions for you?

I’ve never had a club owner tell me a musical prowess such as that, but I’ve had club owners asking is there a way that we could beef up the lineup. Now, the first gig I ever had in my life, in New York as a leader was at the Village Vanguard. I went up to the owner, Lorraine Gordon, and said, “I’d like to work the Vanguard.” And she said, “Well listen, who’s going to be in your band?” I said, “Well let me make some phone calls.” Well I knew Ron Carter, not as well as I know him now but I knew him to a point that…

I think that’s really interesting in that sometimes when you see a new artist and you see the cast of supporting characters in it, like wow, I always thought that that probably came from the record company. Like you need to have this to help sell your first.
